chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): that he asked him.

About a man who performed Umrat al-Tamattu' and had no sacrificial animal (hady), so he fasted three days in Dhu al-Hijjah, then died after returning to his family before fasting the seven days. Is it upon his guardian to make up for him? He said, 'I do not see it obligatory upon him to make up.' If he returned to his family, he must fast these seven days, and it is not permissible for him to give charity on his behalf with his choice. He narrated that.

key_terms.عُمْرَةُ التَّمَتُّعِ: Umrat al-Tamattu' (Umrah performed with the intention of combining it with Hajj)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on fasting for a pilgrer who died before completing the compensatory fast of Umrat al-Tamattu'?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the compensatory fasting for Umrat al-Tamattu' is a personal obligation (fard 'alayhi) rather than a debt of the body, meaning death does not necessitate the guardian to fast on the deceased's behalf. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential distinction between obligations that transfer to heirs and those that remain strictly personal, emphasizing the pilgrim's direct responsibility to complete the seven days upon returning home.
